subject.title: fix(agents): tombstone permanently dead OAuth refresh grants so external CLI login can re-seed the profile

question: Does direct inspection of the sibling Codex credential-store implementation confirm that a changed refresh token is a safe and sufficient boundary for re-seeding a dead OpenAI profile?
rationale: OpenClaw policy makes this a required dependency-contract gate for Codex-related OAuth behavior, and the required direct source inspection was unavailable rather than disproven.

options.title: Confirm and proceed
options.body: Inspect the exact Codex auth-store and refresh behavior; if it matches the PR’s assumptions, accept the focused recovery design.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: If Codex can rotate or represent grants in a way that invalidates token-string comparison, request a contract-safe identity or fingerprint boundary before merge.

recommendation.title: Confirm and proceed
recommendation.body: Inspect the exact Codex auth-store and refresh behavior; if it matches the PR’s assumptions, accept the focused recovery design.

likelyOwner.reason: They can supply implementation context and update the branch, although repository-history ownership could not be established here.
